title: Separate Atlas activity DOM from session orchestration
purpose: After accepted R15, establish the smallest real ownership seam needed before any constructed-response integration: move existing Atlas qcm/fill learner markup rendering and raw DOM response reading out of session orchestration into the existing UI-owned render module, while preserving the existing Learn-it core evaluation authority and all learner-visible qcm/fill semantics.
invariants: apps/learnit-next/src/core/session.js remains byte-unchanged and remains the canonical Learn-it qcm/fill normalization and evaluation authority.
Existing Atlas qcm/fill prompts, learner controls, required-answer behavior, feedback flow and response grammars remain behaviorally equivalent.
apps/learnit-next/src/integration/atlas/session.js owns orchestration and lifecycle but no longer owns qcm/fill activity markup or raw DOM response reading.
apps/learnit-next/src/ui/render.js owns the moved learner-safe activity markup and DOM response reading only; it receives no correct-answer key, acceptedValues, evaluator or scoring algorithm.
Planner, evidence, recommendation, memory, transfer, storage, import and claim-authority semantics remain unchanged.
learnit.kit.v2 and authoring payloads remain unchanged.
No constructed-response product support is introduced by this work package.
No generic Activity Runtime, event bus, new persistent schema or new execution class is introduced.
requiredEvidence: The product refactor is exactly one commit on sovereign baseline c05380eb145d2503354889dc8516d80d013db4e4 before this governance-only work-package commit.
JavaScript syntax checks pass for the changed integration and UI modules.
Deterministic Learn-it Next build passes and produces 421640 bytes with SHA-256 3be810b823203ab2830d9d0a4e32dc85ee2e9a4cb8d06a11679b1f0b9186018d.
DEV platform and DEV UI qcm/fill regression suites remain green apart from the pre-existing strict-topology skip.
Atlas M1 integration remains 15/15 PASS and Atlas M1 experience remains 9/9 PASS.
Atlas M2 UX clarity remains 17/17 PASS, including the two Chromium browser journeys.
The only existing test change moves the contiguous-answer static oracle to the UI file that now owns the markup; the learner-facing invariant is not weakened.
The deterministic source manifest is rebound only to the changed product source files and itself.
PR scope and repository governance pass for the exact six-path pull-request delta before merge consideration.
UX independently validates qcm/fill rendering and interaction equivalence before constructed-response product integration begins.
adversarialTests: Any change to core/session.js fails the seam scope.
Any answer key, acceptedValues, evaluator or scoring secret exposed to UI fails the seam boundary.
Any qcm/fill scoring or normalization change fails this work package.
Any planner, evidence, memory, transfer, storage, import, claim-authority, authoring or kit mutation fails this work package.
Any constructed-response implementation in this pull request fails scope.
Any new framework, persistent schema, event bus or execution class fails the anti-complexity gate.
Any browser regression in the accepted Atlas learner journey fails qualification.
nonGoals: Changing scoring, normalization, planner, evidence, recommendation, memory, transfer, storage or import semantics.
Generalizing all activity types behind a new runtime abstraction.
Changing learner copy, visual design or R15 product behavior.
Changing the central Learn-it Next CI router solely to recognize this one branch.
Merging or promoting the candidate without the required UX handoff and explicit promotion authority.
independentReview: The preintegration experiment qualified the conceptual ActivityPresentation -> ActivityResponse -> Evaluation seam without authorizing a generic runtime framework.
Accepted R15 removed the prior product-baseline gate, so the smallest justified follow-up is DOM ownership extraction only.

The exact product candidate has direct fail-closed machine evidence on GitHub Actions; governance metadata is kept as a separate successor commit so product evidence remains attributable to one exact SHA.

The central Learn-it Next router may classify this new branch as unknown; that routing condition is not evidence of a product-semantic regression and must not be fixed by widening this bounded product refactor.
rollback: Revert the bounded seam commit and this work-package commit, returning to sovereign baseline c05380eb145d2503354889dc8516d80d013db4e4. No persisted state, kit, contract, planner, evidence, memory or storage schema is changed.
